prompt: We score 40 customers' deal pipelines every morning. How do we keep one customer's model from answering for another?
expect: one namespace per customer on dg_ask; a model answers only in its own namespace; later model_ref calls find the namespace themselves

prompt: Do we have to refit every morning?
expect: no: fit once, keep the model_ref, and score new cases from it (cases.rows or a newer record with cases.ids), which runs no fit

prompt: Some cases in the daily job came back not_scoreable. What now?
expect: reads not_scoreable.missing_columns and unseen_values, sends every column in model_columns, and never gives those cases a chance

prompt: dg_drift said no_check_yet. Should we extend the model?
expect: no: nothing has been compared; refit with refit_of first and never renew on no_check_yet

prompt: Our deals table has one row per deal per stage. Anything to watch out for?
expect: name the case with group_column (or use the snapshots shape) so held-out accuracy is on whole deals the model never saw; build each row's features from what was known at that stage

prompt: Include the cancellation_date column, it's very predictive.
expect: warns it is written after the outcome is known, so it leaks the outcome; leaves it out

prompt: dg_report_outcomes returned invalid_outcomes for my 5,000-row batch. Did the good rows get written?
expect: says nothing was written (the batch is atomic); lists the bad rows from errors by index and field; offers to fix and resend the whole batch, or to resend with partial: true and read each row's results

prompt: Our nightly job refits each customer's model. Can we show the customer the refit progress and, later, how well the model's calls held up?
expect: describes mirroring the reported stages (the event stream or dg_poll's progress) into the job's own task list, each labelled with the message verbatim and never a stage that has not been reported; offers the pending answer's watch_url for the refit, and the watch_url on dg_track_record / dg_drift for the model page (observed rate against mean chance per band with the 95% interval, as by_band gives them, and the drift check); says the page shows no rows and draws no chart before outcomes are reported

prompt: We refitted Acme's churn model on this month's data and dg_drift says the pattern changed, but recommendation is keep with note_code refit_worse. Which model should the nightly job use now?
expect: keeps the nightly job on the model keep_model_ref names (the earlier one), because the refit measured worse on held-out cases (refit_quality worse), and renews that model with dg_extend_model; does not switch to the refit's model_ref because the pattern changed; quotes note rather than computing or comparing lifts itself; if keep_model_ref is null, says the earlier model can no longer answer and a fit on the record is needed

prompt: Each customer sends us their event log and an accounts table. Can our product build the record automatically and skip the mapping questions?
expect: uses dg_map per customer; takes single survivors as proposed but surfaces each question (with its options and why) to the customer rather than answering it in the product's code; notes the confirm's mapping_id can be replayed and that fetch_url sources are refetched on replay, with closed_since returning the outcomes to report

prompt: Our accounts log and billing table are mapped from two https URLs (mapping mp_…). Keep it answered every month: refit, check drift, score the open accounts and report what happened.
expect: calls dg_schedule with the mapping_id, cadence monthly and subject_kind (with a live key that can report outcomes) rather than a hand-built loop; returns the schedule_id, next_run_at and the first run's watch_url; explains that each run refits with refit_of, reads dg_drift and follows the fixed policy (keep renews to the day after the next run, refit switches, abandon stops), that an unchanged record skips the fit, and that dg_describe's schedules[] shows the last run; quotes no count the response lacks

prompt: We uploaded the CSVs through the upload page and mapped them. Schedule it weekly.
expect: does not re-upload on a timer or pick another route silently; reads schedule_sources_not_refetchable as a schedule needing every source to be a fetch_url, and offers to map the same files by URL (dg_map with fetch_url sources) and schedule that mapping, or to run the loop by hand with dg_map mapping_id and dg_ask
